title: Grid Navigation, Data Entry & AutoFill
description: Learn Excel workbook layout, cell coordinate references (A1, B2), text/number entry, and AutoFill handles.
objectives: Navigate spreadsheet grid rows (1,2,3) and columns (A,B,C)
Enter numeric values and text strings into active cells
Use AutoFill handle to populate date and number series

steps.title: The Excel Grid & Formula Bar
steps.content: Excel stores data in a grid of columns (letters) and rows (numbers). Cell intersections (like A1 or B3) hold data or formulas. The formula bar (fx) displays cell contents.

steps.title: Interactive Challenge: Enter Data into Cell A1
steps.content: Select cell A1 in the interactive Excel grid below and enter the numerical value 250.
steps.hint: Click cell A1 at the top-left of the grid and type '250'.

quiz.question: How is a specific cell address referenced in Microsoft Excel?
options: Column Letter followed by Row Number (e.g. B4)
Row Number followed by Column Letter (e.g. 4B)
quiz.explanation: Excel cell coordinates start with the Column letter followed by the Row number (e.g. B4).

title: Essential Formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE, =COUNT, =MAX)
description: Write basic formulas starting with '=' to perform mathematical calculations across cell ranges.
objectives: Understand why all Excel formulas begin with '='
Calculate range totals using =SUM(A1:A3)
Compute statistical averages using =AVERAGE(B1:B10)

steps.title: Writing Formulas in Excel
steps.content: Every formula in Excel must begin with an equals sign (=). For example, =SUM(A1:A3) adds up all values from cell A1 down to A3.

steps.title: Interactive Challenge: Insert SUM Formula
steps.content: Click the AutoSum button on the ribbon or type =SUM(A1:A3) in cell A4.
steps.hint: Click cell A4 and click AutoSum (∑) on the Home tab ribbon.

quiz.question: Which character must precede every calculation formula in Excel?
quiz.explanation: The equals sign (=) tells Excel to treat the cell contents as an executable formula.

title: Logical & Conditional Functions (=IF, =AND, =OR, =IFS)
description: Master conditional decision-making logic using nested =IF statements and multi-condition =IFS.
objectives: Build conditional test rules using =IF(test, true_val, false_val)
Combine logical rules with =AND and =OR
Simplify multi-branch criteria with =IFS

steps.title: Conditional Business Logic
steps.content: The =IF function tests whether a condition is met (e.g. Sales > 5000) and returns one result if TRUE, and another if FALSE.

quiz.question: What will =IF(10>5, 'Pass', 'Fail') evaluate to in Excel?
quiz.explanation: Since 10 is greater than 5, the TRUE branch result 'Pass' is returned.

title: Advanced Lookup Functions (=VLOOKUP, =INDEX/MATCH, =XLOOKUP)
description: Search master tables to auto-fill pricing, customer info, and inventory data across worksheets.
objectives: Search vertical tables using =VLOOKUP
Combine =INDEX and =MATCH for flexible two-way lookups
Utilize modern =XLOOKUP for simplified, robust data retrieval

steps.title: Lookup & Reference Automation
steps.content: =VLOOKUP and =XLOOKUP automatically search a product ID or employee code in a master table and return corresponding price or salary details.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of modern =XLOOKUP over legacy =VLOOKUP?
options: =XLOOKUP can search data to both the left and right without requiring column index numbers
quiz.explanation: =XLOOKUP is flexible and can look up data in any direction without static column index offsets.

title: Data Sorting, Filtering & Conditional Formatting
description: Filter large data tables, apply multi-level sort orders, and highlight top performers with color scales.
objectives: Apply AutoFilters to headers for quick criteria searching
Sort data alphabetically or numerically by multiple keys
Highlight cells dynamically using Conditional Formatting rules

steps.title: Visual Data Highlighting
steps.content: Conditional formatting automatically applies green background fills to cells exceeding targets or red highlights to overdue tasks.

quiz.question: Which tool dynamically changes a cell's fill color based on its value?
quiz.explanation: Conditional Formatting applies rules to change text or background color depending on cell values.

title: Interactive Charts, Graphs & Sparklines
description: Create Column, Bar, Line, and Pie charts, edit chart axes, and insert in-cell Sparkline mini-graphs.
objectives: Select data series and generate Column and Line charts
Format chart titles, legends, and data labels
Embed tiny trend Sparklines directly inside grid cells

steps.title: Visual Data Visualization
steps.content: Charts summarize numeric trends visually for business executive reports. Sparklines render tiny trendlines inside single cells.

quiz.question: Which chart type is best suited for showing proportion parts of a whole 100% total?
quiz.explanation: Pie charts illustrate proportional distribution parts of a single whole total.

title: PivotTables, Slicers & Data Validation Pro
description: Summarize tens of thousands of data rows instantly with PivotTables, visual Slicers, and Drop-down input menus.
objectives: Create interactive PivotTables to aggregate raw data
Add visual Slicer buttons for instant filtering
Restrict cell inputs with Data Validation drop-down menus

steps.title: Summarizing Data with PivotTables
steps.content: PivotTables aggregate thousands of data rows into clean summary tables with interactive filtering slicers, cross-tabulation, and pivot charts.

quiz.question: Which feature provides clickable visual filter buttons for interactive PivotTable dashboards?
quiz.explanation: Slicers add visual buttons to filter PivotTable data instantly.

title: Power Query, Financial Models & VBA Macros Pro
description: Automate data ETL pipeline imports using Power Query, build financial forecast models, and write VBA Macros.
objectives: Clean and transform raw data using Power Query
Perform sensitivity analysis with What-If Goal Seek
Write custom VBA code to automate entire workbook workflows

steps.title: Power Query & Automation Engine
steps.content: Power Query extracts data from external databases or CSV files, cleans messy rows, and loads refreshed tables into Excel automatically.

quiz.question: Which built-in Excel tool is designed for importing, cleaning, and transforming messy raw datasets?
quiz.explanation: Power Query is Excel's robust ETL data transformation and cleaning engine.
